2022 / Research Story

Tracing a skin-aging signal from HDAC4 to DDIT4

Lee et al. Aging (Albany NY). 2022;14(11):4653-4672.

Methods in this study
  • Primary human dermal fibroblasts
  • UV / oxidative-stress senescence models
  • Bulk RNA-seq + public transcriptome integration
  • Gene overexpression / knockdown
  • SA-β-gal · qPCR · immunoblotting
  • Human skin immunohistochemistry

01 / The question

The question

Which genes and cellular changes connect reduced HDAC4 to stress-induced senescence in skin fibroblasts?

02 / How we tested it

How we tested it

RNA-seq after HDAC4 overexpression or knockdown in primary human dermal fibroblasts was integrated with public UV- and oxidative-stress senescence datasets. DDIT4 perturbation tested effects on SA-β-gal, SASP and aging-related expression, complemented by analyses of young and aged human skin.

How the evidence connects

This collaborative study combined newly generated HDAC4-perturbation RNA-seq (GSE181329) and experiments with public senescence transcriptomes (GSE60795 and GSE116761).

03 / What the study found

What the study found

DDIT4 knockdown reduced the senescence-modulating effect of HDAC4, while DDIT4 overexpression improved several senescence-associated readouts. Lower DDIT4 expression in aged human skin provided tissue-level support for further investigation of the HDAC4–DDIT4 pathway.

04 / Interpreting the evidence

Interpreting the evidence

The evidence comes from cell models and comparisons of human skin across age groups. It does not establish clinical rejuvenation, and the precise mechanism linking HDAC4 to DDIT4 expression remains to be resolved.

Figures from the paper

Figure 2A–B shows integrative candidate selection; Figure 6A shows DDIT4 immunohistochemistry in human skin. The gene-perturbation experiments are not shown in these images.

The next question

A question to explore together

How does the HDAC4–DDIT4 response vary with donor age and UV history, and can the effect be validated at the tissue level?
